newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy mkt sees o/n rate falling slightly.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy mkt sees o/n rate falling slightly.

text.p: Italy money market expectations for an easing in rates are slightly greater than a week ago, a study by the Bocconi University research arm Igier showed.

Last week the market showed its disappointment at a lack of an official rate cut by the Bank of Italy amid heightened uncertainty over the future of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), seeing an upturn in market rates.

But this week Italian markets reacted positively to the new political scenario in France and to policy wrangles in Germany between Bonn and the Bundesbank, despite Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio's comments cooling hopes of an early rate cut.

On a one-month timeframe, the market sees the implicit overnight rate standing at 6.87 percent from 6.92 percent last week and 6.78 percent two weeks ago. On Thursday, the day on which the study is based, the rate stood at 6.96 percent.

On a one-year time frame the implicit o/n rate is seen at 6.46 percent against 6.60 percent last week and 6.44 percent one month ago. On a two-year horizon the implicit o/n rate is seen standing at 6.64 percent from 6.85 percent last week.

The spread between Italian and German implicit o/n rates, considered a good indicator of market confidence of Italy joining EMU, this week stood at 200 basis points from 205 bps last week. One month ago the spread was at 232 bps and one year ago at 245 bps.
